newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR - Over 1,500 Hutu returnees arrested in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR - Over 1,500 Hutu returnees arrested in Rwanda.

text.p: More than 1,500 Hutu refugees returning home to Rwanda from Tanzania have been arrested on charges of taking part in 1994's genocide, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday.

The agency expressed concern over the situation in Rwanda's southeastern Kibungo region where it said 1,000 Hutus had been arrested. Another 520 were held in Murambi village in the northern region of Nyagatare, where 15,000 people died in the genocide.

UNHCR said there was growing tension between returnees and the locals in Kibungo, where in some villages the returnees outnumbered the residents. Two returnees had committed suicide and five genocide survivors had been poisoned.
The arrests included Hutus who had turned themselves in for protective custody to avoid possible retribution by genocide survivors, the UNHCR said.

Nearly two million Hutus fled Rwanda for neighbouring countries in fear of retribution for the Hutu-led genocide of half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates, after which ethnic Tutsis swept to power.
In the past week, up to 300,000 Hutus in Tanzania were forced back home by Tanzanian troops, joining some 650,000 others forced to flee eastern Zaire by ethnic Tutsi rebels.
"The local authorities do not have the capacity to deal with the problems that are arising -- arrests, public order, house occupation, land occupation, health problems and registration," UNHCR said.
Rwandan prisons are so full with genocide suspects that food depots have been turned into jails and the International Committee of the Red Cross has had to help build tent prisons.
Some 90,000 Hutus accused of genocide are jammed into jails and village lock-ups, up from 18,000 in early 1995. The start of trials has been repeatedly delayed.
Few suspects have case files and authorities have forgotton where, when and by whom many were arrested.
